title: Boss Battle: Production Friday
story: The release archive arrived with debug logging, a non-executable deploy script, and a stale watcher holding the old release open. Naturally, the change calendar says this should take five minutes.
objective: Restore /backups/release.tar into /deploy. In the restored app, set LOG_LEVEL to info, set deploy.sh to mode 750, and stop stale release-watcher PID 9001 without stopping metrics-agent PID 9002.
hints: Break the incident into outcomes: extract, edit, set permissions, then stop the stale process.
Restore the archive first with tar -xf release.tar -C /deploy, then use status to see which outcomes remain.
Change only LOG_LEVEL in /deploy/app/app.env. sed -i can replace debug with info in place, or vi can edit the virtual file.
Set /deploy/app/deploy.sh to mode 750, then stop PID 9001 while leaving metrics-agent PID 9002 running.
A complete route is: tar -xf release.tar -C /deploy; sed -i 's/LOG_LEVEL=debug/LOG_LEVEL=info/' /deploy/app/app.env; chmod 750 /deploy/app/deploy.sh; kill 9001. Enter each command separately.
explanation: Real incidents combine independent faults. Work from observable outcomes, verify each change, and avoid collateral damage: restore the files, make the narrow config edit, grant only needed permissions, and terminate only the stale process.
